title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Yb3+ luminescent SMMs are harder to realize than Dy3+ analogues because the smaller J lowers doublet axiality, and a large mismatch between the magnetic barrier and the luminescence gap means under-barrier processes dominate.
explanation: Yb3+ is the second most used ion for luminescent SMMs because of NIR 2F5/2 → 2F7/2 emission, but pure Ising mJ = ±7/2 ground states are not always obtained. In one TTF/beta-diketonate dimer the magnetic barrier (15 cm−1) matches the ±7/2 to ±5/2 gap (16 cm−1); another TTF complex (4 vs 234 cm−1) and the trensal complex (26 vs 464 cm−1) show much smaller magnetic barriers, so QTM, Raman, or direct paths, not a simple Orbach model, govern relaxation. A large spectroscopic splitting is still viewed as a target if under-barrier paths can be removed.
scope: Yb3+ complexes with beta-diketonate/tetrathiafulvalene or tripodal Schiff-base ligands.
conditions: Field-induced or weakly blocked Yb3+ SMMs; crystal-field gaps from luminescence, sometimes with EPR and calculations.
caveats: Some related Yb complexes are not SMMs because the ground state is not pure Ising. The very large spectroscopic gaps are not realized as magnetic barriers in the cited systems.
